question: What proportion of phenotypic dihydride modified by double dominant epistasis occurs in a cross AaBb x AaBb ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "AaBb x AaBb" -> "9 genotypes with at least one dominant allele at both loci" -> "3 genotypes with dominant allele at one locus" -> "4 genotypes with recessive alleles at both loci" -> "9:3:4" -> 60%

CHAIN: "AaBb x AaBb" -> "12 genotypes with at least one dominant allele at either locus" -> "3 genotypes with dominant allele at one locus" -> "1 genotype with recessive alleles at both loci" -> "12:3:1" -> 90%
CHAIN: "AaBb x AaBb" -> "9 genotypes with at least one dominant allele at both loci" -> "7 genotypes with recessive alleles at both loci" -> "9:7" -> 50%
CHAIN: "AaBb x AaBb" -> "15 genotypes with at least one dominant allele at either locus" -> "1 genotype with recessive alleles at both loci" -> "15:1" -> 70%
analysis: In a dihybrid cross AaBb x AaBb, double dominant epistasis occurs when the presence of at least one dominant allele from either of the two gene pairs masks the expression of the other gene. This results in a phenotypic ratio of 15:1, where 15 represents the phenotypes showing the dominant trait due to epistasis, and 1 represents the recessive phenotype.
